{
  "research_question": "How does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) affect mouse navigation performance metrics including Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stimulation Paradigm as the fixed factor.",
    "For 'Success', which is binary (0/1), treat it as a proportion and use a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with a binomial distribution and logit link instead of standard ANOVA to handle non-normality and bounded data.",
    "For the remaining continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD), verify normality of residuals and homogeneity of variances before proceeding with F-tests.",
    "If assumptions are violated for continuous variables, apply appropriate transformations (e.g., log for skewed Time-to-Target) or use non-parametric alternatives (Kruskal-Wallis)."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If the omnibus ANOVA/GLM test is significant for a variable, conduct pairwise comparisons between all five stimulation paradigms.",
    "Calculate mean differences and 95% confidence intervals for each pair.",
    "Report p-values adjusted for multiple testing using the strategy defined in 'multiple_comparison_strategy'."
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Apply the False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction (Benjamini-Hochberg procedure) to control the expected proportion of false positives across the set of all pairwise comparisons for each response variable, balancing Type I error control with statistical power given the large sample size (n=76,655).",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Since the response variable 'Success' is categorical (binary), an Ordinary Linear Regression is inappropriate. A Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with a Binomial family and Logit link function (Logistic Regression) is recommended to model the probability of success as a function of the stimulation paradigm. For the continuous variables, a standard Linear Mixed Model (LMM) is recommended to account for the repeated measures structure implied by the 'Mouse' factor (8 levels) listed in the dataset overview, treating 'Mouse' as a random effect to generalize beyond the specific mice in this sample.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality of residuals for continuous outcomes (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) assessed via Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests.",
    "Homogeneity of variances (homoscedasticity) assessed via Levene's test or Bartlett's test.",
    "Independence of observations (verified by experimental design context).",
    "Linearity of the relationship between predictors and the log-odds of success for the GLM.",
    "Absence of multicollinearity among predictors (not applicable here as only one categorical predictor is used in the primary model)."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Based on summary statistics, the 'Sham' paradigm is expected to show significantly lower Success rates (mean=0.27) and higher Time-to-Target (mean=4.68) compared to all other paradigms.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm is expected to yield the highest Path Efficiency (mean=0.50) and Average Speed (mean=12.83), suggesting synergistic effects.",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) is expected to be lowest in the 'Sham' group (mean=0.24) compared to others, indicating less precise navigation without stimulation.",
    "Visual-only paradigms (Dim, Bright) are expected to show intermediate performance, with 'Dim Visual Only' showing notably lower Success (0.67) than 'Bright Visual Only' (0.78).",
    "ICMS Only is expected to show performance closer to Combined but potentially with higher Time-to-Target than Combined."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset includes a large number of mice (8 levels), but the summary does not explicitly state if 'Mouse' was treated as a random effect in the provided summary statistics; ignoring this could inflate Type I error rates if data are clustered by mouse.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary, violating the normality assumption required for standard ANOVA, necessitating a switch to GLM.",
    "Skewed distributions are evident in 'Time-to-Target' (min=0.5, max=201.39) and 'Path Efficiency' (min=0.0009), which may require transformation or non-parametric tests.",
    "Potential confounding variables (e.g., mouse age, strain differences beyond the 8 levels, session order) are not accounted for in the primary one-way analysis."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMM) for each continuous response variable and a Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Model (GLMM) for 'Success', including 'Stim Paradigm' as a fixed effect and 'Mouse' as a random intercept, to properly account for the hierarchical data structure and obtain more robust inference."
}
